morphology_entries.coding_note: Generated by build/generate_group_inventory.py --group VII from ICCC-2017.sqlite joined to icdo32.sqlite, run via build/generate_group07_entries.py; never transcribed from the REDCap option file or the diagnostic pathway document (contract §1, §0.3). ICD-O-3.2 preferred term 'Neoplasm, malignant'. VIIc at C22.0/C22.1 (ICCC-2017 row 72). Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, rule 5, p. 03: a case diagnosed without pathology and outside Tables 3 and 4 is 8000/3. The tree also emits it where two current sources leave the code undecided -- hepatocellular neoplasm NOS (contract §3.3) -- and where a small cell undifferentiated tumour has no INI1 result (contract §4.3). diagnostic_tests_required is Histology and IHC, so an imaging-only 8000/3 shows tissue as outstanding and a small cell undifferentiated tumour with no INI1 result shows IHC as outstanding; with Histology alone the second read 'Workup: complete' above an upgrade line naming INI1 (found driving the INI1 step in the browser, 2 October 2026). The REDCap list also offers 8000/6 and 8000/9 readings, outside this group (contract §2D).

decision_trees.tree_label: Hepatic tumours (C22.0 liver, C22.1 intrahepatic bile duct; ICCC-3 Group VII declares behaviour 3 only) — the hepatoblastoma imaging route at basis 2, the INI1 fork between hepatoblastoma and malignant rhabdoid tumour, the hepatocellular carcinoma subtypes with fibrolamellar carcinoma on 8171/3, combined and biliary carcinomas, undifferentiated embryonal sarcoma, and the referrals out of the group

nodes.question: A child with a liver (hepatic) mass. What is actually in this patient's file?
nodes.hint: Pick the highest tier of evidence genuinely in the file. When the file holds both a biopsy taken before chemotherapy and a resection taken after it, code from the biopsy: after chemotherapy about 20% of hepatoblastomas show areas that mimic hepatocellular carcinoma (López-Terrada 2025, p. 27).
nodes.coding_note: Contract §4. Five routes, the Group 5 and 6 document_inventory idiom. primary_site is captured 'C22' on every option because the whole tree is entered for a liver mass; 8963 and 8991 are Group VII codes only at C22.0/C22.1 (ICCC-2017 rows 68, 69), and the 8963 rules at the INI1 step condition on this capture (contract §3.4, check_group7_c22_only_codes). 'Cytology' in evidence_tests follows Group 6 rn_document_inventory; it is not in the diagnostic_tests_required vocabulary, so no entry requires it and it never suppresses a requirement.

options.label: Referral letter or clinical note only — no imaging report, no cytology, no histology report in the file
Ultrasound, CT or MRI report, with or without a serum alpha-fetoprotein result — no tissue (cytology or histology) in the file
Histology report from a needle or wedge biopsy, a resection, a transplant hepatectomy or an autopsy
Fine-needle aspiration or other cytology report only — no histology report in the file
A specimen was taken but is reported inadequate, non-diagnostic or uninterpretable

nodes.question: What does the referral letter or clinical note say?
nodes.hint: A note alone never registers a specific liver tumour. Visser 2023, Table 3 (pp. 04–05), allows hepatoblastoma to be registered without pathology at basis 2 — clinical investigation, including imaging — and not on a note. A malignancy that the note says is at least likely is recorded as Neoplasm, malignant (8000/3) at basis 1 until the imaging and pathology reports are found (Visser 2023, rule 5, p. 03).
nodes.coding_note: Deviation from Group 6 rn_clinical_alias, recorded in the build report: Group 6 sends a referral-only case on to its imaging node, where a case with no imaging report cannot tick the constellation and its insufficient node offers no honest option. Here the note itself decides: a malignancy stated as at least likely is 8000/3 at basis 1, which Visser rule 5 (p. 03) allows and rule 4 bounds; anything less is not registered. No specific Group VII code is emitted at basis 1 (contract §0.6 point 2). Registrar item: contract §11.

options.label: The note states that a malignant liver tumour is likely — for example 'hepatoblastoma', 'hepatocellular carcinoma', 'liver cancer' or 'malignant liver mass'
options.reason: A note cannot register a specific liver tumour: hepatoblastoma needs at least clinical investigation, basis 2 (Visser 2023, Table 3). Visser rule 5 (p. 03) records a malignancy that is at least likely, on clinical grounds alone, as Neoplasm, malignant (8000/3), here at the liver in this group's unspecified subgroup. Find the imaging and pathology reports and code the case again — they will give a more specific code.
options.upgrade_path: The imaging report, the alpha-fetoprotein result and any pathology report. Each can move this case from Neoplasm, malignant to a specific code.

options.label: The note describes a liver mass or abnormal findings without saying a malignancy is likely, or names a non-malignant cause that could equally explain them — haemangioma, abscess, hydatid or simple cyst, hepatitis, a storage disease
options.reason: Under Visser 2023, rule 4 (p. 03), a case where cancer is only possible, or where a non-malignant disorder could equally explain the findings, is not registered without pathology.

nodes.question: No tissue exists. Tick what the imaging report and the laboratory report actually state, then answer the checklist below.
nodes.hint: Both boxes must be true for the hepatoblastoma route to count. The international consensus recommends a biopsy for every child with a liver tumour, whatever the age or alpha-fetoprotein (López-Terrada 2014, p. 484); registering a case without one rests on Visser 2023, Table 3, which allows hepatoblastoma at basis 2. A normal or low alpha-fetoprotein does not exclude hepatoblastoma — leave that box unticked and the case goes to tissue.
nodes.coding_note: imaging_sufficient true on 8970/3 only (contract §4.2); basis 2 per Visser Table 3, pp. 04-05 (registrar item §11.4a: whether alpha-fetoprotein raises it to 4 under rule 1). The constellation is the Design Specification §3.6 row: large hepatic mass, child <3, raised AFP. Age is asked as two diversion criteria, not built into the constellation, because imagingPathway() requires every imaging_features box ticked and a box the clerk cannot read off the report makes the route unreachable (Group 6 contract §0.8b). The lower bound is 6 months on Ferraro 2019, PDF p. 7; the pathway document says 4 (registrar item §11.5). Every diversion cites the paper and page in its clerk-facing reason. No satisfies_tests: 8970's entry requires Histology, and the consensus asks for a biopsy in every patient (López-Terrada 2014, p. 484), so histology stays outstanding on this terminal rather than being suppressed — the opposite choice to Group 6's 8960 imaging terminal, recorded in the build report.
imaging_features: A solid mass arising within the liver on ultrasound, CT or MRI

biochemical_questions.question: Serum alpha-fetoprotein is reported raised above the laboratory's reference range for the child's age

diversion_criteria.feature: The child is 3 years of age or older
diversion_criteria.reason: Hepatoblastoma is generally diagnosed under 3 years (López-Terrada 2025, p. 24). In an older child, hepatocellular carcinoma, hepatocellular neoplasm NOS and embryonal sarcoma enter the differential, and imaging with alpha-fetoprotein does not separate them. Tissue is required.

diversion_criteria.feature: The infant is younger than 6 months
diversion_criteria.reason: Alpha-fetoprotein is physiologically very high in early infancy, and reference intervals vary so widely up to at least 6 months that a single value cannot be read as raised for age (Ferraro 2019, PDF p. 7). Tissue is required.

diversion_criteria.feature: The mass is predominantly cystic or multicystic
diversion_criteria.reason: Undifferentiated embryonal sarcoma often looks cyst-like on CT and MRI (Salles-Silva 2025, p. 173), and mesenchymal hamartoma is solid and cystic with an alpha-fetoprotein that can be moderately raised (López-Terrada 2025, p. 39). Tissue is required.

diversion_criteria.feature: The radiologist favours a vascular lesion, such as a haemangioma
diversion_criteria.reason: Haemangioma is the most common vascular liver tumour of childhood (López-Terrada 2025, p. 33), and alpha-fetoprotein is raised in about 14% of them (Ferraro 2019, Table 4, PDF p. 10). Tissue is required.

diversion_criteria.feature: The child has chronic liver disease — cirrhosis, biliary atresia, tyrosinaemia, progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis or chronic hepatitis B
diversion_criteria.reason: These are the conditions in which paediatric hepatocellular carcinoma arises (López-Terrada 2025, Table 2, p. 29), and imaging with alpha-fetoprotein does not separate it from hepatoblastoma. Tissue is required.

diversion_criteria.feature: A mass is also described outside the liver — gonad, sacrococcygeal region, mediastinum, adrenal gland or kidney
diversion_criteria.reason: The liver lesions may be metastases. Alpha-fetoprotein is raised in over 90% of yolk sac tumours (Ferraro 2019, Table 4, PDF p. 10). Tissue is required, and the case may belong to another group.

nodes.reason: A solid liver mass with alpha-fetoprotein raised for age, with neither age diversion ticked (younger than 6 months, or 3 years or older) and no other feature that requires tissue. Recorded as Hepatoblastoma, NOS (8970/3) at basis 2, clinical investigation (Visser 2023, Table 3, pp. 04–05).
nodes.upgrade_path: A diagnostic biopsy, which the international consensus recommends for every child with a liver tumour (López-Terrada 2014, p. 484), would confirm hepatoblastoma and exclude malignant rhabdoid tumour, hepatocellular neoplasm NOS and hepatocellular carcinoma. The hepatoblastoma subtype it reports refines risk and does not change the code.

nodes.step_label: Imaging did not confirm — what next
nodes.question: The imaging route did not confirm hepatoblastoma: a feature requiring tissue applies, or a box was not true. What does the file show?
nodes.hint: Do not code a specific tumour from the imaging report's wording. A biopsy is where this case goes; it is not certain to settle it.
nodes.coding_note: Reached only from hp_imaging_pathway's insufficient_next_node, which carries no captures of its own (Group 6 rn_imaging_insufficient coding_note), so the first option's label requires an imaging report rather than assuming one: a case that entered on the inadequate-specimen route may have none. Visser 2023, rule 5 (p. 03) for the 8000/3 option; rule 4 (p. 03) for the non-reportable option.

options.label: An imaging report is in the file, there is no diagnostic tissue, and the report or the clinical team states that a malignant liver tumour is likely
options.reason: Recorded as Neoplasm, malignant (8000/3), this group's unspecified malignant hepatic subgroup at the liver, pending a diagnostic specimen. Visser 2023, rule 5 (p. 03), records a case diagnosed without pathology as 8000/3. Visser's Table 3 (pp. 04–05) also allows hepatocellular carcinoma and cholangiocarcinoma at basis 2, and its Table 4 (p. 06) allows hepatocellular carcinoma on alpha-fetoprotein; this tool codes both only on tissue, and the registrar's ruling on a no-tissue route for them is outstanding.

options.label: The findings could equally be explained by a non-malignant lesion — haemangioma, mesenchymal hamartoma, focal nodular hyperplasia, an abscess, a hydatid cyst or a simple cyst
options.reason: Under Visser 2023, rule 4 (p. 03), a case where a non-malignant disorder could equally explain the findings is not registered without pathology.

options.label: Tissue has since been obtained — a histology report is now in the file
Tissue has since been obtained — a cytology report only is now in the file

nodes.question: What does the fine-needle aspiration or other cytology report show?
nodes.hint: Fine-needle aspiration is not recommended for liver tumours in children because it samples too little tissue to classify them (Ng & Mogul 2018, PDF p. 7). Code a specific tumour only when the cytology report itself makes that diagnosis.
nodes.coding_note: ENCR basis 5 for cytology (Visser 2023, Table 1, p. 03). The hepatoblastoma option excludes small cell undifferentiated and rhabdoid cells, because those need an INI1 result that a smear does not carry (contract §4.3). A non-diagnostic smear returns the case to the imaging route, where hepatoblastoma can still be registered at basis 2, rather than ending at 8000/3 basis 9 as Group 6's rn_cytology does.

options.label: The cytology report diagnoses hepatoblastoma, with no small cell undifferentiated or rhabdoid cells described
options.reason: Cells diagnostic of hepatoblastoma on cytology, basis of diagnosis 5. A smear cannot establish the subtype, which does not change the code. Recorded as Hepatoblastoma, NOS (8970/3).

options.label: The cytology report diagnoses hepatocellular carcinoma
options.reason: Cells diagnostic of hepatocellular carcinoma on cytology, basis of diagnosis 5. Recorded as Hepatocellular carcinoma, NOS (8170/3); a subtype needs histology.

options.label: Malignant cells are present, but the report does not name the tumour type, or names a small round cell or rhabdoid tumour
options.reason: Malignant cells on cytology without a stated type. A small round cell or rhabdoid tumour in the liver could be hepatoblastoma or malignant rhabdoid tumour, and only INI1 on tissue separates them. Recorded as Neoplasm, malignant (8000/3) at the liver pending histology.

options.label: The cytology is non-diagnostic, scant or shows no malignant cells

nodes.question: What does the histology report diagnose?
nodes.hint: Code from the report's own diagnosis. Hepatoblastoma subtype — pure fetal, crowded fetal, embryonal, pleomorphic, cholangioblastic, macrotrabecular, mixed epithelial and mesenchymal, teratoid — never changes the code. A small cell undifferentiated tumour, or any tumour with rhabdoid cells that the report does not call a malignant rhabdoid tumour, is decided by INI1 and SMARCA4 at the next step.
nodes.coding_note: Contract §4. Entity list from the International Pediatric Liver Tumors Consensus Classification as reproduced in López-Terrada 2025, Table 1, p. 24. Hepatoblastoma subtypes all 8970/3 (pp. 24-25). Small cell undifferentiated or rhabdoid predominance must not emit 8970 without INI1 (Vokuhl 2016, p. 925; check_group7_ini1_fork). Hepatocellular neoplasm NOS has no ICD-O-3.2 code (contract §3.3). cHCC-CCA is H&E-defined (Brunt 2018, manuscript p. 2). UESL needs no marker panel (López-Terrada 2025, p. 36). CNSET is 8975/1, or 8975/3 under the matrix rule when the report calls it malignant or describes metastases (registrar ruling, 3 October 2026; contract §3.1). Referrals: sarcomas to IX (8910 IXa, 9120/9133 IXd8, 9040 IXd7, 8806 IXd11, 9140 IXc, all any-site in ICCC-2017); germ cell tumours at C22 to Xb (rows 124, 126); lymphoma to II; leukaemia, including the acute megakaryoblastic leukaemia López-Terrada 2025 Table 1 lists among liver masses, to I. Benign lesions on a Group VII code stem (8170/0, 8160/0, 8148/2) are behaviour exclusions; benign lesions with no Group VII stem are non-reportable.

options.label: Hepatoblastoma — fetal, embryonal, pleomorphic, cholangioblastic or macrotrabecular epithelial pattern, mixed epithelial and mesenchymal, or teratoid — with no rhabdoid cells described and no small cell undifferentiated component predominating
options.reason: Hepatoblastoma on histology. Every epithelial and mixed subtype is the same code; the subtype refines risk (López-Terrada 2025, pp. 24–25). Recorded as Hepatoblastoma, NOS (8970/3).

options.label: A small cell undifferentiated (blastemal) pattern predominates, with no rhabdoid cells described
The report diagnoses a malignant rhabdoid tumour
options.reason: The pathologist diagnoses a malignant rhabdoid tumour. Rhabdoid tumour is still diagnosed on its histomorphology (López-Terrada 2014, p. 479), and a rhabdoid tumour that keeps INI1 is a recognised entity (López-Terrada 2025, Table 1, p. 24; Vokuhl 2016, p. 927). Recorded as Rhabdoid tumor, NOS (8963/3), a Group VII code at the liver only, on the report's diagnosis.
options.upgrade_path: INI1 (SMARCB1) immunohistochemistry, if it is not in the file, would confirm the diagnosis; the code stays Rhabdoid tumor, NOS whatever it shows.
options.coding_note: Added after review, 3 October 2026. A report that DIAGNOSES malignant rhabdoid tumour is coded on that diagnosis, not routed through INI1: before this split, an INI1-retained malignant rhabdoid tumour reached the 8970 rule and was recoded as hepatoblastoma with 'Workup: complete' (Vokuhl 2016, p. 927, case 17: typical rhabdoid morphology, INI1 retained, classed malignant rhabdoid tumour). No satisfies_tests: 8963 requires IHC, and nothing on this path records it, so IHC shows as outstanding. Registrar item in docs/group_07_open_questions.md.

options.label: The report diagnoses hepatoblastoma and also describes rhabdoid cells in it, without calling the tumour a malignant rhabdoid tumour
Rhabdoid cells are described, and the report names no tumour type — neither hepatoblastoma nor a malignant rhabdoid tumour
Hepatocellular carcinoma, including fibrolamellar carcinoma
Hepatocellular neoplasm NOS (HCN-NOS), hepatocellular malignant neoplasm NOS, or a hepatocellular tumour the report places between hepatoblastoma and hepatocellular carcinoma
options.reason: The international consensus created this provisional category for tumours with features of both hepatoblastoma and hepatocellular carcinoma; these children are treated as high-risk hepatoblastoma (López-Terrada 2025, pp. 29–31). ICD-O-3.2 has no code for it, and the two candidates — Hepatoblastoma, NOS (8970/3) and Hepatocellular carcinoma, NOS (8170/3) — sit in different ICCC subgroups. Recorded as Neoplasm, malignant (8000/3) at the liver until the registrar rules.
options.coding_note: satisfies_tests IHC: the consensus diagnosis rests on beta-catenin immunohistochemistry, which is universally nuclear positive in this category (López-Terrada 2025, p. 31), so a report that makes it has done IHC. 8000's entry requires Histology and IHC; without this the panel would show IHC as outstanding on a case whose diagnosis is defined by it.
options.upgrade_path: No more specific code exists yet. The registrar is to rule between Hepatoblastoma, NOS (8970/3) and Hepatocellular carcinoma, NOS (8170/3) for this category; re-code the case when they do.

options.label: Combined hepatocellular-cholangiocarcinoma — hepatocellular and cholangiocellular differentiation intimately mixed in one tumour, not two separate tumours
options.reason: Combined hepatocellular-cholangiocarcinoma is diagnosed on routine histology; immunostains support it but are not essential (Brunt 2018, manuscript p. 2). Two separate tumours in one liver are a collision, not this diagnosis. Recorded as Combined hepatocellular carcinoma and cholangiocarcinoma (8180/3).

options.label: Cholangiocarcinoma, or another carcinoma of the bile ducts
Undifferentiated embryonal sarcoma of the liver
options.reason: Undifferentiated embryonal sarcoma is diagnosed on its histology alone; no immunohistochemical marker is diagnostic (López-Terrada 2025, p. 36). Recorded as Embryonal sarcoma (8991/3), which is a Group VII code at the liver only.

options.label: Calcifying nested stromal-epithelial tumour (also called nested epithelial stromal tumour or ossifying stromal-epithelial tumour), with no statement that it is malignant and no metastases described
options.reason: ICD-O-3.2 codes this tumour 8975/1, uncertain whether benign or malignant. Group VII otherwise registers malignant tumours only; this one is registered at behaviour 1 by the registrar's ruling of 3 October 2026. Most patients have a benign course after complete excision; some relapse or metastasise (López-Terrada 2025, p. 43). If a later report calls it malignant or finds metastases, the code becomes 8975/3.
options.upgrade_path: A later report that calls the tumour malignant, or finds metastases, changes the behaviour to 3 (8975/3).
options.coding_note: Registrar ruling 3 October 2026, open question 2(a). Replaces the behaviour exclusion.

options.label: Calcifying nested stromal-epithelial tumour (also called nested epithelial stromal tumour or ossifying stromal-epithelial tumour), and the report calls it malignant or describes metastases
options.reason: The pathologist reports this tumour as malignant, or it has metastasised. ICD-O-3.2 lists it only as 8975/1, uncertain whether benign or malignant; ICD-O's matrix rule permits changing the behaviour digit to what the pathologist reports, which gives 8975/3, and ICCC-2017 places 8975/3 in Group VII, subgroup VIIa1. Recorded as Calcifying nested stromal-epithelial tumor, behaviour 3, by the registrar's ruling of 3 October 2026. Most patients have a benign course after complete excision; some relapse or metastasise (López-Terrada 2025, p. 43).
options.coding_note: Registrar ruling 3 October 2026, open question 2(b). check_group7_cnset keeps 8975/3 on this label only.

options.label: Another sarcoma — embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma of the liver or bile ducts, angiosarcoma, epithelioid haemangioendothelioma, synovial sarcoma, desmoplastic small round cell tumour, or Kaposi sarcoma
options.reason: These are soft tissue sarcomas wherever they arise, and ICCC-3 places them in Group IX, soft tissue and other extraosseous sarcomas. Embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma of the bile ducts is the commonest malignant cause of obstructive jaundice in childhood (López-Terrada 2025, p. 38) and is coded there, not here.

options.label: A germ cell tumour — yolk sac tumour, teratoma or a mixed germ cell tumour
options.reason: ICCC-3 places a germ cell tumour arising outside the gonads and the central nervous system in Group X, subgroup Xb, at any site including the liver.

options.label: Lymphoma, or another lymphoid or histiocytic neoplasm involving the liver
options.reason: Lymphomas and reticuloendothelial neoplasms are ICCC-3 Group II wherever they arise.

options.label: Leukaemia infiltrating the liver, including acute megakaryoblastic leukaemia presenting as a liver mass
options.reason: Leukaemias are ICCC-3 Group I. Acute megakaryoblastic leukaemia is listed among the tumours that present as a liver mass in children (López-Terrada 2025, Table 1, p. 24).

options.label: A metastasis from a tumour arising elsewhere
Another carcinoma — adenocarcinoma, a neuroendocrine tumour or carcinoma, NUT carcinoma, undifferentiated carcinoma, or a carcinoma whose lineage the report does not state
Hepatocellular adenoma

behaviour_exclusion.reason: Hepatocellular adenoma is a benign tumour, coded 8170/0 in ICD-O-3.2, where it is listed as liver cell adenoma. It shares its four digits with hepatocellular carcinoma, 8170/3, but ICCC-3 Group VII admits behaviour 3 only, so no Group VII code is emitted. If the report describes malignant change in the adenoma, choose hepatocellular carcinoma instead.

options.label: Bile duct adenoma

behaviour_exclusion.reason: Bile duct adenoma is a benign tumour, coded 8160/0 in ICD-O-3.2. It shares its four digits with cholangiocarcinoma, 8160/3, but ICCC-3 Group VII admits behaviour 3 only, so no Group VII code is emitted.

options.label: Biliary intraepithelial neoplasia, high grade (BilIN-3), or high-grade glandular dysplasia with no invasive carcinoma

behaviour_exclusion.reason: High-grade biliary intraepithelial neoplasia is an in situ lesion. ICD-O-3.2 codes it 8148/2, glandular intraepithelial neoplasia, high grade, and has no behaviour-3 code for it. ICCC-3 Group VII admits behaviour 3 only, so no Group VII code is emitted. If the report describes invasion, choose the carcinoma instead.

options.label: Another benign, premalignant or non-neoplastic lesion — haemangioma, mesenchymal hamartoma, focal nodular hyperplasia, a macroregenerative or dysplastic nodule, a cyst or an abscess
options.reason: A benign, premalignant or non-neoplastic liver lesion is not a reportable malignancy. The international consensus lists mesenchymal hamartoma, haemangioma and focal nodular hyperplasia among the benign liver lesions of childhood, and dysplastic nodules as premalignant (López-Terrada 2025, Table 1, p. 24).

options.label: A malignant tumour, but the report does not establish its type
options.reason: Malignancy confirmed on histology without a stated type. Recorded as Neoplasm, malignant (8000/3), this group's unspecified malignant hepatic subgroup at the liver.

nodes.step_label: INI1 — hepatoblastoma or malignant rhabdoid tumour
nodes.question: Record the INI1 (SMARCB1) result, and the SMARCA4 (BRG1) result if it was done.
nodes.hint: INI1 decides the code, and SMARCA4 decides it when INI1 is retained. INI1 lost: malignant rhabdoid tumour — 22 of 23 tumours first diagnosed as small cell undifferentiated hepatoblastoma or malignant rhabdoid tumour had lost it (Vokuhl 2016, p. 925). INI1 retained: a small cell undifferentiated pattern, or rhabdoid cells in a hepatoblastoma, does not make the tumour a malignant rhabdoid tumour unless SMARCA4 is lost; about 5% of rhabdoid tumours keep INI1 and lose SMARCA4 instead (López-Terrada 2025, p. 37). Record SMARCA4 if it was done; if it was not, the code is given with IHC still outstanding. INI1, SMARCB1, BAF47 and SNF5 name the same protein; SMARCA4 is also called BRG1.
nodes.coding_note: Contract §4.3, the group's signature fork. Retention is its own POSITIVE marker, not a negative requirement on the loss marker, because app.js markerOff() satisfies a negative requirement with a marker that was never recorded (line 1220) — a 'not lost' rule written that way would code an untested tumour as hepatoblastoma, the error Vokuhl 2016 documents. Marker wording follows Group 3 st_embryonal_family. The SMARCA4 rule precedes the retention rule, so a tumour with INI1 retained and SMARCA4 lost reaches 8963. The 8963 rules condition on primary_site C22 (ICCC-2017 row 68; check_group7_c22_only_codes). INI1 not done falls to 8000/3 (ruling 11: the nearest code that does not overstate). Rebuilt 3 October 2026 on the registrar's ruling (open question 18): INI1 retained with SMARCA4 retained is not a malignant rhabdoid tumour; the code follows the report's own diagnosis; SMARCA4 not recorded gives the same code with IHC outstanding through outstanding_tests. nodes.question: Which hepatocellular carcinoma does the report name?
nodes.hint: Code the subtype the report names. If the report places the tumour between hepatoblastoma and hepatocellular carcinoma, or calls it a hepatocellular neoplasm NOS, go back one step and choose that instead: those tumours are nuclear β-catenin positive and are not treated as hepatocellular carcinoma (López-Terrada 2025, pp. 30–31).
nodes.coding_note: ICD-O-3.2 carries five hepatocellular carcinoma subtype codes inside ICCC-2017 row 71, none of them a REDCap option yet (contract §2B): 8171 fibrolamellar, 8172 scirrhous, 8173 spindle cell, 8174 clear cell, 8175 pleomorphic. Fibrolamellar goes through the molecular node because a negative test can move it to 8170 (contract §3.2). Subtypes ICD-O-3.2 does not code separately stay on 8170.

nodes.question: What does the report say about molecular testing for fibrolamellar carcinoma?
nodes.hint: Fibrolamellar carcinoma is coded 8171/3 on its morphology. The DNAJB1::PRKACA fusion transcript was found in every fibrolamellar carcinoma tested and in no other liver tumour type, and PRKACA FISH was negative in all six scirrhous hepatocellular carcinomas tested (Graham 2015, p. 822). In the Carney complex PRKAR1A is lost instead (Graham 2018, PDF p. 2). A negative test changes the code only when the report itself revises the diagnosis.
nodes.coding_note: Contract §3.2. Basis 8 where a fusion or PRKAR1A loss is found (Visser rule 10: the abnormality is specific to the entity); basis 7 otherwise. The one code change: a report that revises the diagnosis to hepatocellular carcinoma with fibrolamellar-like features after negative testing — BAP1-inactivated mimics lack the fusion (López-Terrada 2025, p. 29). Gene names render verbatim (ruling 10).
